chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: Buying Jan Garber's library written by Spud Murphy
summary: Before the Paramount band he bought Jan Garber's library for twenty dollars, and only about 25 arrangements were usable.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, incidentally, when I started my first band, you know, going -- before the Paramount, I bought Jan Garber's library for twenty bucks, when he changed over to the Guy Lombardo thing?

And Spud had written most of those arrangements. It was a sort of a pseudo-swing band, you know. It wasn't the -- the only part was that Spud never wrote any parts for himself, because he had them in his head, having written the arrangements. And I got all of these arrangements. I was able to -- oh, there must have been a couple of hundred arrangements. There was a trunk full of
music and -- every one -- I got maybe 25 arrangements out of there that were playable, because -- that Spud hadn't written.
That's funny. Didn't he also write for Benny Goodman?

Yes, he wrote for Benny Goodman. He wrote for a lot of people. Spud was a very good arranger. He's still around, up in the union. He has some capacity up there, I don't know exactly what. He's on one of the boards or committees, one of the elder statesmen.
Yeah. I think he's about 70 by now.
